paper.title: SkillWeaver: Web Agents can Self-Improve by Discovering and Honing Skills
paper.central_claim: A web agent can self-improve without parameter updates by autonomously proposing skills for a new website, practising them, synthesizing them into Python/Playwright APIs and honing them with tests; the resulting library raises success on WebArena (relative +31.8%) and on live websites (+39.8%) and transfers to weaker agents (up to +54.3%).

evidence.quote: Given a new website, the agent autonomously discovers skills, executes them for practice, and distills practice experiences into robust APIs.
evidence.support_explanation: Core loop: self-proposed skill tasks, practice, API synthesis; no test queries or demonstrations are used.

evidence.quote: we emphasize skill diversity by explicitly prompting LLMs to propose novel and reusable skills beyond the current skill repertoire.
evidence.support_explanation: Curriculum is a prompted LLM proposal of procedural, navigational and information-seeking tasks conditioned on the skill library and observations; no measured test that the novelty prompting or simple-to-complex progression matters.

evidence.quote: We prompt an LLM to provide reward signals indicating task completion success with the following observations in the context:
evidence.support_explanation: Admission of a practised trajectory is decided by an LLM reward model (task, trajectory with screenshots, execution feedback); its accuracy is not measured.

evidence.quote: from successful trajectories into a reusable and generalized API.
evidence.support_explanation: Successful trajectories are converted to Python functions with signature, docstring, usage log and prerequisite-state description; a static analyser rejects common generation mistakes.

evidence.quote: For APIs requiring no extra parameters except the by default Playwright page instance, we execute the API directly as a standalone unit test.
evidence.support_explanation: Honing executes each API as a unit test (with LLM-generated parameter values where needed) and debugs it from feedback.

evidence.quote: was to have it be called without producing an exception, we found that occasionally, malfunctioning APIs could be marked as verified simply because they silenced all exceptions that could have occurred.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors report that the honing criterion is 'runs without exception', so an API that suppresses errors can pass; the update_product_quantity example shows this. Correctness of retained skills is therefore not guaranteed.

evidence.quote: iterations with GPT-4o, where an iteration is defined as either attempting a proposed skill or testing an existing skill.
evidence.support_explanation: Exploration budget: 160 iterations per website with GPT-4o, run per website separately before evaluation; during exploration the agent can call earlier APIs to compose new ones.

evidence.quote: Task success rate on WebArena. The numbers in green represent the relative improvement percentage.
evidence.support_explanation: GPT-4o baseline agent avg 22.6 (Gitlab 17.8, Map 27.5, Shopping 19.8, CMS 18.7, Reddit 37.7) to 29.8 with skills (22.2, 33.9, 27.2, 25.8, 50.0), relative +31.9%. GPT-4o-mini 9.2 to 14.1 (+53.3% by our computation; the table's last cell says 45%). Absolute gains are 4-12 points per site on 106-187 tasks, single run.

evidence.quote: Our experiments on WebArena demonstrate consistent performance improvements with the integration of synthesized APIs. As illustrated in Table
evidence.support_explanation: The same paragraph states '39.8% on average' for GPT-4o on WebArena, while Table 1 and the abstract give 31.8-32%; 39.8% is the live-website figure. The reported improvement figures are inconsistent across abstract, text and table.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.1, comparison with AutoEval and SteP
evidence.quote: achieves higher average success rates and exhibits better or comparable performance across all domains, with the exception of the Shopping environment.
evidence.support_explanation: Compared with numbers taken from other papers with different base agents: AutoEval avg 26.9 (Shopping 39.6) vs SkillWeaver+Skills 29.8; SteP, which uses human-written workflows, has avg 33.0 and is higher overall; SkillWeaver is higher only on Map (33.9 vs 30.0) and CMS (25.8 vs 24.0).

evidence.quote: To ensure the validity of evaluation, we manually evaluate the success of agent trajectories.
evidence.support_explanation: Live-website evaluation is manual by the authors. Table 2: Drug 65.0 to 87.0 (15 to 20 of 23), Flight 11.7 to 29.4 (2 to 5 of 17), Cooking 62.5 to 75.0 (5 to 6 of 8), Car 11.1 to 11.1 (1 of 9); in total 23 to 32 of 57 tasks, single run, +9 tasks; no blinding stated.

evidence.quote: Considering the cost of exploration on all the websites, we only consider websites with a sufficient number of tasks that can be accessed by Playwright.
evidence.support_explanation: Only 4 of 136 websites and 57 of 300 tasks were evaluated; exploration cost is cited as the reason but no cost number is given anywhere in the paper.

evidence.quote: adapt the agent to different websites by purely integrating synthesized API libraries generated during pre-hoc website explorations.
evidence.support_explanation: Test tasks are not used for skill construction; the library is built in a separate exploration phase per website, giving a task-disjoint build/evaluate split. The text does not state whether the website state is reset after exploration, though exploration executes side-effecting skills (e.g. deleting merged branches).

evidence.quote: We conduct a comparative experiment by replacing the backbone language model with GPT-4o-mini without any other modification to the agent.
evidence.support_explanation: GPT-4o-synthesized libraries are consumed by a GPT-4o-mini agent (9.2 to 14.1 avg), showing the artifact is transferable across executors.

evidence.quote: This result suggests that our exploration process is capable of generating APIs with quality that is comparable to or even superior to manually crafted APIs found in official documentation.
evidence.support_explanation: Result is shown only in Figure 3 (no numbers in text); synthesized APIs are said to match human APIs on Reddit and Shopping and to be worse on GitLab and Maps.

evidence.quote: Given the extensive number of synthesized APIs, we introduce an API selection module that filters only relevant APIs from the API library.
evidence.support_explanation: An extra LLM call selects relevant skills per task and filters by pre-conditions; its contribution and cost are not ablated.

evidence.quote: LLMs like GPT-4o are still not robust enough at API calling, and that hurts API-augmented agents like ours, even with human-crafted APIs.
evidence.support_explanation: Stated failure categories: not identifying the right API, wrong parameters; Appendix D.2.4 shows an agent not calling an available API at all.

evidence.quote: However, its natural language-based routines pose challenges for formal verification and precise composition into new workflows.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap against AWM and ICAL: text routines are unverifiable and hard to compose; and those methods use test queries or annotated demonstrations. Neither is run as a baseline.

evidence.quote: If a task attempt was successful , you may create a skill to simplify the task .
evidence.support_explanation: Knowledge-base update prompt: successful attempts add a skill; failed attempts that used a skill lead to documentation updates; docstrings carry a usage log; updates replace a function with the same name. No retirement, versioning or size bound.

evidence.quote: We implement a web agent with only browsing actions based on CodeAct
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline is the same CodeAct agent without skills (22.6 avg), so skills-on/off is the comparison; there is no baseline given the same exploration compute through another mechanism (memory, workflows, retries).

evidence.support_explanation: GPT-4o-2024-08-06 at temperature 0.3, 10 steps; single run per cell, no seeds, intervals or tests anywhere in the paper.

evidence.quote: After a certain number of exploration iterations, we observe that the pipeline begins to generate
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative observation that later APIs call earlier ones (compositional skills); no count or ablation of composition.

evidence.quote: For example, screenshot and HTML files consume approximately 0.3 GB per trajectory with an average of 7.3 actions in Mind2Web
evidence.support_explanation: Author motivation: trajectory-based memory is heavy to store and share, favouring compact API artifacts.

signatures.object: Per-website skill library of async Python/Playwright APIs with docstrings (usage log, pre-conditions); baseline is the CodeAct agent with atomic browser actions only.
signatures.information: Screenshots, accessibility tree, URL and page state; own prior skill list and semantic knowledge notes; LLM-judged success; execution exceptions. No test queries or demonstrations.
signatures.operation: (I) LLM proposes a new short-horizon skill task (procedural, navigational, information-seeking) beyond the current repertoire; (II) agent attempts it, LLM reward model judges success, successful trajectories are converted to an API and statically checked; (III) each API is run as a unit test with LLM-chosen parameters and debugged; docstrings are updated after later attempts.
signatures.output: Library of callable skills, 160 exploration iterations per website with GPT-4o, composable by later skills.
signatures.conditions: Website where short, reusable procedures exist; LLM judge and test inputs adequate; agent able to call APIs.
signatures.feedback: LLM reward on trajectories; Python exceptions and environment feedback in honing.
signatures.selection_rule: Retain if the reward model says success and the API runs without exception in the unit test; update by function-name replacement.
signatures.persistence: Library files per website, reused at inference via an API selection module that filters by relevance and pre-conditions; shareable across agents.
signatures.later_use: Skills added to the agent's action space at evaluation time and also used in later exploration for composition.
signatures.claimed_effect: WebArena avg 22.6 to 29.8 (GPT-4o) and 9.2 to 14.1 (GPT-4o-mini); live 23 to 32 of 57 tasks.
signatures.failure_boundary: Exception-free is accepted as verified (D.2.1); no realistic test inputs for data-dependent skills (D.2.2); weak LLMs mis-select or mis-parameterise APIs; high-API-support sites favour human APIs.

signatures.object: Skill-use interface: API selection module that filters the library per task and checks pre-conditions.
signatures.information: Task description, current state, skill signatures and docstrings.
signatures.operation: LLM selects candidate functions and injects 'signature + docstring' into the prompt.
signatures.output: Task-conditioned skill list for the acting agent.
signatures.conditions: Library too large for full inclusion.
signatures.claimed_effect: Enables use of a large library; not ablated.
signatures.failure_boundary: Failure to call available APIs (D.2.4) and wrong parameters (D.2.5).

gap.author_gap: Web agents lack autonomous self-improvement: trajectory-memory and fine-tuning approaches do not abstract reusable procedures and are heavy to share; AWM and ICAL use natural-language routines that resist verification and composition and depend on test queries or annotated demonstrations.
gap.checked_gap: The target is specific: label-free, query-free exploration producing verifiable, composable, shareable artifacts. The protocol difference from AWM/ICAL is real, but those neighbours (and the concurrent ASI work of overlapping authors) are not run, and the quantified headroom is only the skills-off baseline.
gap.lineage: Voyager-style skill libraries and LLM curricula -> Agent Workflow Memory / ICAL (text routines) -> SkillWeaver (self-proposed tasks, verified executable APIs, portability). Comparisons are to AutoEval and SteP using published numbers. Neighbours cited, not available as fixed local sources.
gap.closest_adjacent: AWM, ICAL, Synapse (trajectory exemplars), Voyager, AutoEval, SteP.
gap.residue: Reliable verification of synthesized skills, test inputs for data-dependent skills, robust skill calling, high-API-support sites.
gap.stakes: Adaptation of web agents to unfamiliar websites without supervision or parameter updates.
gap.method_response: Executable API artifacts built by a propose-practise-synthesise-hone loop and shared across agents.
gap.remaining_gap: Verification relies on exception-free runs and an LLM judge; skill-use failures dominate the residual errors; cost is unmeasured.
unresolved: Whether AWM/ICAL-style or test-time retry baselines at equal exploration compute match the library could not be checked from fixed local sources.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A skill library built by task-agnostic autonomous exploration (160 GPT-4o iterations per website) raised the same agent's success on unseen WebArena tasks from 22.6 to 29.8 average and on 57 manually judged live-website tasks from 23 to 32 successes, and the GPT-4o-built library also helped a GPT-4o-mini agent (9.2 to 14.1); all single runs without intervals. The role of the discovery curriculum, reward model and honing stage, the cost of exploration, and the advantage over text-routine or retry baselines are not shown.

G.reason: The objective (query-free exploration producing verifiable, composable, shareable skills) is concrete and the protocol difference from AWM and ICAL is argued, but those neighbours and the concurrent ASI are not run, comparisons use other papers' numbers, and the residual error sources are only illustrated.

M.reason: Propose-practise-synthesise-hone is a coherent, reconstructable mechanism and error-driven repair is documented, but the assumptions that the novelty curriculum and LLM reward model select good skills are untested and the honing check accepts exception-free code, as the authors' own failure case shows.

X.reason: Prompts, hyperparameters, library format with pre-conditions and usage logs, the selection module and the persistence prompt are fully given, and failure modes (silent-exception APIs, missing test inputs, skill-calling errors) are reported openly; retirement, versioning, library size and website-state reset are absent.

E.measurement.reason: The 812-task WebArena programmatic checker is a credible main metric; live-site results are manually judged by the authors on 57 tasks without blinding, the reward model and honing verifier are unvalidated, and relative-improvement figures are inconsistent across abstract, text and table.

E.causality.reason: Skills-on/off on two agents and two benchmarks establishes that the retained library carries the gain, but no ablation tests discovery, reward filtering, honing, composition or API selection, no equal-compute alternative (text workflows, retries), and the SteP/AutoEval comparisons use external numbers.

E.holdout.reason: Skills are built by task-agnostic exploration and evaluated on unseen WebArena and live tasks, with transfer to a different executor; remaining gaps are no explicit overlap or contamination check, unspecified website-state reset, and an unspecified prompt-tuning set.

E.statistics.reason: Task counts are given and a null result (Car) and SteP's higher score are visible, but every number is one run at temperature 0.3 with no intervals, seeds or tests, and the live-site gain is nine tasks.

E.cost.reason: No token, call, time or monetary cost is reported for 160 exploration iterations on each website, honing, or the per-task API selection, although cost is invoked to limit the live evaluation.
